newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares mixed to firmer in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares mixed to firmer in active trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares opened the week mixed to firmer in active trade on Monday, driven largely by a spate of company results released last week and a couple of broker presentations, brokers said.

They however said volumes were still rather small as major institutional investors continued to sit on the sidelines watching new issues leaving smaller investors and unit trusts doing a bit of portfolio balancing the main market players.
"Generally the market is mixed and it's being driven by recent results and broker presentations. The major institutions are still on the sidelines looking at new issues," one broker said.
The key industrial index put on 10.08 points to close at 10,372.69, pushed up by merchant banker FMB's 200 cent rise to 4,700 and timber producer Border 's 150 cent gain to 1,200.

Soft drinks manufacturer Schweppes jumped 50 cents to 410, tobacco company TSL added 20 cents to 700 as did glass firm PGI to 660 while seed manufacturer and distributor Seedco put on 15 cents to 300 and cement producer Porthold gained 10 cents to 1,650.

Among the day's losers, publishing group Zimpapers retraced some of its gains last week, dropping 200 cents to 5,300 while 50 cent cuts were recorded in pharmaceutical group Caps to 1,200, engineering firm Gulliver to 350 and hotel and supermarket company Meikles to 2,650.
Minings were lacklustre with prices showing little conviction either way. Nickel producer Bindura and gold counters Rio Tinto and Falgold were unchanged while Ashanti slid 500 cents to 9,500.
The mining index eased a marginal 1.75 points to 989.56.
